source.title: Entropy-MCMC: Sampling from Flat Basins with Ease

record.tranche_reason: The study measures flatness with Hessian approximations and parameter interpolation, then reports test performance, but it does not use the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments compare flatness-aware sampling and optimization methods on test metrics and examine flatness measures. None tests the claim versions as written: cited findings about sharpness and generalization are prior work, and the study does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop Entropy-MCMC and evaluates its performance. Its diagonal-Fisher eigenspectra and Euclidean interpolation do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps against competing measures. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Entropy-MCMC efficiently samples flat basins and that explicitly considering flatness can improve generalization, robustness, and uncertainty estimation under practical computational constraints. These are the authors' conclusions, not a demonstrated test of V7.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes an auxiliary-variable MCMC sampler using SGLD; the claim versions concern other interventions, comparisons, and measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracy varies by dataset and sampling method; appendix ablations also report effects of temperature, variance parameter, step-size schedule, and sample-set composition.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy-MCMC reaches 95.69% and 79.16% accuracy on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, versus SGD's 94.87% and 76.49% and SGLD's 95.47% and 78.79%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested recipes, Entropy-MCMC Bayesian predictions improve classification accuracy over these SGD and SGLD baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: On ResNet18/CIFAR100, EMCMC has smaller diagonal-Fisher eigenvalue estimates and lower, flatter training-NLL and test-error interpolation curves than SGD and SGLD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EMCMC produces flatter local geometry under the study's diagnostics alongside better test performance; these diagnostics do not establish V7.

record.problems: The flatness analysis uses the diagonal Fisher information matrix as an approximation to the Hessian eigenspectrum. Flatness comparisons use last samples, and the parameter interpolation findings are presented as figures without numerical values. Training and test errors are not reported together in the main CIFAR classification table.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 1 baseline-method rows, corrupted CIFAR results, ImageNet results, OOD detection results, calibration results, and appendix ablations were not extracted because they do not test a listed version and exceed the focused rows selected for findings outside the versions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization using the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test error gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note; uses_without_test/T4 fits the supplied text. No qualifying results were found beyond the rows. The performance and geometry rows can remain as findings outside the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error after widening beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps; the study uses different flatness measures and does not compare networks at similarly low training loss.
